title: 7 Best Macaly Alternatives for Building Apps with AI in 2027

body_markdown:
Macaly offers AI-powered app creation for founders and small businesses, but the best platform depends on whether you need mobile publishing, team collaboration, or managed infrastructure.[Floot](https://floot.com/) is one option for building and hosting full-stack apps through an existing AI assistant.


This guide compares seven Macaly alternatives for non-technical founders, small teams, and agencies in 2027. It covers how each platform handles app building, publishing, pricing, and ownership, including options that work directly with Claude or ChatGPT.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Bring your existing AI subscription** : Floot connects to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Codex via MCP, so connector-based building uses your existing AI subscription and Floot's plan-based build-action limits rather than a second AI build-credit bill. Hosting and optional AI features have separate allowances and charges.
- **Floot's mobile publishing** : Floot packages web apps into iOS and Android shells (2 builds/month on Free, 12/month on Pro, unlimited on Power). App-store publishing requires developer accounts and is subject to store review.
- **Team costs depend on collaboration models** : Floot Pro starts at[$25/month](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for the project owner, while collaborators building through their own MCP connections need their own paid Floot plans.
- **Full-stack infrastructure reduces setup** : Floot provides managed Postgres, authentication, file storage, and hosting, reducing the need to configure separate services.
- **Code ownership enables flexibility** : Floot users own their code and data on every plan. Database export is available on all plans, while full project ZIP export requires a paid plan.


## **Understanding AI App Builders in 2027**


AI app builders have evolved beyond simple website generators into platforms capable of creating full-stack applications with databases, user authentication, payment processing, and mobile deployment. According to Precedence Research, the global[low-code AI platform market](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/low-code-ai-platform-market) is projected to grow from $7.85 billion in 2026 to $56.82 billion by 2035, at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 24.6%.


This growth is driven by increasing demand for faster application development, generative AI integration, and tools that enable non-technical users to build functional applications through natural language interfaces. As these platforms evolve, several key capabilities have become essential for building and deploying applications effectively:


- **Conversational Development:** Build applications using natural language prompts with AI assistants like Claude or ChatGPT.
- **Backend Infrastructure:** Access managed databases, user authentication systems, and other essential backend services.
- **Deployment and Hosting:** Publish applications to custom domains with CDN-backed hosting and delivery.
- **Mobile Capabilities:** Convert web applications into iOS and Android apps for distribution through app stores.
- **Integration Ecosystems:** Connect applications to payment processors, analytics platforms, and third-party APIs.


Macaly, acquired by team.blue in December 2025, offers a free tier and a $25/month Pro plan with managed hosting, authentication, and database features. In September 2026, Macaly also introduced Macaly Cloud, an MCP-connected service that enables app development through Claude and ChatGPT. However, teams evaluating mobile publishing workflows, collaboration costs, and managed app infrastructure may find that different alternatives better suit their specific needs.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions. The Y Combinator-backed platform (Summer 2025 batch) serves non-technical builders using conversational app development.


### **Key Capabilities**


- **MCP connector for AI assistants** : Build through supported Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, and Cursor configurations using your existing AI subscription
- **Three build paths** : Choose between the[Claude/ChatGPT connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , an in-app editor with optional Floot AI agent, or code editor integration with Cursor
- **Managed Postgres database** : SQL access, browser-based table view, and[database export](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) on every plan
- **Built-in authentication** : Email/password login plus Google and Microsoft OAuth brokering without separate OAuth app setup
- **Native mobile builds** : Package web apps as installable iOS/Android shells with[store publishing support](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/publishing-to-app-stores) for TestFlight and Google Play testing tracks


### **Why Floot Works for Business Apps**


Floot supports multiple application types. Non-technical founders can build MVPs for booking systems, customer portals, and e-commerce applications. Small business owners can create internal tools for employee management, inventory tracking, and client dashboards. Agencies can build customized applications for clients, with the option to remove Floot branding on paid plans.


One[G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/floot/reviews) reports building an e-commerce experience in under a month.


### **Organizational Fit**


Floot offers three pricing tiers. The Free plan includes 100 build actions per day, 2 mobile builds per month, and a one-time $3 hosting credit. Pro costs[$25/month](https://floot.com/en/pricing) with 1,000 actions per day, 5,000 monthly AI credits, a $10/month hosting allowance, 12 mobile builds per month, and custom domains. Power costs $100/month with 5,000 actions per day, 15,000 monthly AI credits, a $25/month hosting allowance, and unlimited mobile builds. Build-action allowances reset daily.


Users own their code, data, and IP on every plan.[Project collaboration](https://floot.com/docs/projects/sharing-your-projects) requires a paid plan, and collaborators building through their own MCP connections need their own paid accounts. Annual plans offer two months free.


### **Building with Existing AI Assistants**


Floot's connector uses your existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription for code generation. This avoids a separate Floot AI build-credit charge for ordinary connector work, although plan fees, hosting usage, image generation, and optional Floot AI agent features may still incur costs. The[preview and annotation tools](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/editor-and-preview) let users point to elements and mark up screenshots for their AI assistant, and the platform's[managed infrastructure](https://floot.com/docs/getting-started/how-floot-works) provides hosting, databases, authentication, and file storage for full-stack apps.


Floot's managed infrastructure includes[Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , serverless backend endpoints, file storage with CDN delivery, user authentication with OAuth brokering, email and push notifications, and scheduled jobs on paid plans after publication. These managed services reduce infrastructure setup, although some features, including[live payments](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/payments) and production email, require additional configuration.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable is an established AI app builder with a prompt-to-code environment and backend options including Lovable Cloud and Supabase. The platform has built a strong community around its template library and documentation.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Integrated AI environment** : Built-in AI agent for code generation and iteration
- **Backend options** : Database, authentication, and storage through Lovable Cloud or Supabase integration
- **Code export** : TypeScript/React/Tailwind output with GitHub sync
- **Template library** : Pre-built starting points for common application types
- **Community resources** : Extensive documentation and user community


### **App Building Considerations**


Lovable works well for teams building web applications through its integrated AI environment, while also supporting external AI tools through MCP. The platform supports SaaS dashboards, internal tools, and customer-facing web apps through Lovable Cloud or Supabase.


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable suits individual builders and small teams looking for managed web-app infrastructure. The platform uses a credit-based pricing model starting at $25/month for the Pro tier with 100 credits. Teams should compare AI-credit allowances, hosting usage, and collaboration features rather than assume per-user subscription charges.


## **3. Bubble**


Bubble is a widely used visual no-code development platform, reporting 6 million builders and 8 million apps created since 2012. The platform offers extensive visual programming capabilities for complex web applications.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual programming** : Drag-and-drop interface with conditional logic and workflows
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Over 100 plugins for specialized functionality
- **Database and authentication** : Built-in data layer with user management
- **Enterprise features** : SOC 2 report access, governance tools, and dedicated support on Enterprise plans
- **Workload-based pricing** : Capacity scales with application traffic and operations


### **App Building Considerations**


Bubble excels at complex business applications requiring sophisticated workflow logic. Teams use it for CRM systems, marketplace platforms, internal operations tools, and applications needing extensive conditional logic and approval chains.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble suits teams willing to invest time learning its visual programming paradigm. Its visual editor has a learning curve, but Bubble also offers an AI agent and MCP-based building alongside granular control over application behavior. Pricing for web apps with custom domains starts at $32/month billed annually, while mobile and combined web-and-mobile plans have separate pricing.


## **4. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new is a browser-based AI development environment that supports multiple frontend frameworks and prioritizes code portability. The platform supports prompt-based app creation while also giving developers access to generated code.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Multi-framework support** : Works with React, Vue, Next.js, Svelte, and other frameworks
- **Browser-based development** : No local setup required
- **Code export** : Full project download in standard formats
- **Bolt Cloud** : Optional managed hosting with database and authentication
- **Prompt-based building** : Supports natural-language app creation, with code access for users who want more control


### **App Building Considerations**


Bolt.new works well for rapid prototyping where developers want to quickly generate starting code and then customize. The platform supports both simple landing pages and more complex applications when paired with its cloud services.


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new supports non-technical builders working from prompts as well as developers who value framework flexibility and editable code. The platform offers token-based pricing starting at $25/month for the Pro tier.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 is a newer AI app builder positioning itself as beginner-friendly with an all-in-one approach to no-code development. Wix acquired Base44 in June 2025.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Beginner-friendly interface** : Designed for users with no technical background
- **Integrated backend** : Built-in database and authentication
- **Visual editing** : Point-and-click customization alongside AI prompts
- **Template starting points** : Pre-built application templates
- **Wix ownership** : Acquired by Wix in June 2025 and operated as a standalone product


### **App Building Considerations**


Base44 targets app builders creating full-stack web applications, including internal tools, CRMs, client portals, and booking systems.


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 suits solo builders exploring app creation for the first time. It offers a free plan, with paid plans starting at $16/month billed annually or $20/month billed monthly for Starter. Features and usage allowances vary by plan.


## **6. Replit**


Replit is a cloud-based development environment with AI assistance through Replit Agent. The platform combines coding IDE capabilities with deployment infrastructure.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Cloud IDE** : Browser-based coding environment supporting multiple languages
- **Replit Agent** : AI assistant for code generation and debugging
- **Instant deployment** : One-click publishing to Replit-hosted URLs
- **Collaboration** : Real-time multiplayer coding features
- **Learning focus** : Educational resources and community


### **App Building Considerations**


Replit serves both non-technical builders and developers creating full-stack web apps and native iOS apps with Replit Agent. The platform's AI agent assists with code generation, explanation, and debugging.


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit suits builders who want prompt-based app creation alongside access to a cloud coding environment. Its AI agent can generate and publish applications without requiring users to write code. Replit offers a free Starter plan, while Core costs $20/month with monthly billing or $18/month billed annually, with additional usage costs depending on the services consumed.


## **7. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets users create, host, and share websites and lightweight web applications directly through ChatGPT. Users describe what they want, refine the experience conversationally, and publish it through ChatGPT without configuring a separate hosting provider.


### **Primary Focus**


- **ChatGPT-native development** : Create and edit websites and web apps through natural language
- **Managed hosting** : Publish sites to ChatGPT-hosted URLs or connected custom domains
- **Persistent data and authentication** : Support for saved data, file storage, and sign-in options
- **Built-in sharing controls** : Share with selected users, workspaces, or the public, depending on plan permissions
- **Usage-based limits** : Building and editing use Codex allowances, while hosting and storage have separate limits


### **App Building Considerations**


ChatGPT Sites works well for interactive dashboards, team trackers, client portals, resource hubs, and lightweight business applications. It appeals to users who want to create and publish web experiences without leaving ChatGPT.


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites suits individuals and teams already using eligible ChatGPT plans who want a built-in web publishing workflow. Floot is worth considering when users specifically want MCP-connected managed app infrastructure and a workflow for packaging and publishing iOS and Android apps.


## **Why Floot Stands Out Among Macaly Alternatives**


Floot combines development through supported AI assistants with the infrastructure needed to run full-stack applications. Its[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets users create, edit, test, and publish projects while Floot manages hosting and backend services. Building capabilities depend on connector permissions and plan allowances.


- **Mobile publishing** : Floot includes 2 monthly builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power.[Mobile publishing](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) requires no Mac or Xcode through Floot's managed workflow, but store accounts and approval are still necessary.
- **Managed infrastructure** : Floot provides Postgres, authentication, file storage, serverless backends, and configurable payment processing without requiring users to assemble the infrastructure themselves.
- **Code ownership** : Users own their code and data on every plan. Database export is available on all plans, while paid plans include ZIP export for[self-hosting](https://floot.com/docs/projects/self-hosting) , which requires configuring replacement services.
- **SEO capabilities** : Floot provides[SEO settings](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) , optional server-side pre-rendering, sitemap and robots.txt support, page metadata, and visitor analytics.


Floot is free to start, with Pro at[$25/month](https://floot.com/en/pricing) and Power at $100/month. Connector-based building avoids separate Floot AI build-credit charges, while subscription fees, hosting overages, and optional AI features remain part of the overall cost.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is the main difference between Floot and Macaly?**


Floot and Macaly both support building through existing AI assistants. Floot provides an MCP-connected full-stack platform, while Macaly offers its own AI builder and Macaly Cloud for Claude and ChatGPT workflows. Floot also includes iOS and Android mobile builds across its Free, Pro, and Power plans. Both provide managed hosting and databases, so teams should compare building limits, infrastructure allowances, mobile workflows, and collaboration requirements.


### **Can I start building mobile apps on Floot for free?**


Yes. Floot is free to start, and its Free tier includes[2 monthly mobile builds](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , allowing you to package your web app in a native iOS or Android shell without a Mac or Xcode. App-store publishing requires developer accounts ($99/year for Apple and $25 one-time for Google). Connecting Google Play also requires a paid Floot plan, and store approval is subject to Apple's and Google's review processes.


### **Do I own the code and data created with Floot?**


Yes. Floot states that users own their project code, app data, and intellectual property on every plan.[Database export](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) is available on all tiers. Paid plans include the ability to download the full project as a ZIP file for self-hosting elsewhere, although managed services need to be configured or replaced.


### **Does Floot provide SEO tools for AI-built apps?**


Yes. Floot offers optional[server-side pre-rendering](https://floot.com/docs/projects/seo) so search engine crawlers can receive page-specific HTML, titles, descriptions, and content. Users can ask their AI assistant to add and update sitemap.xml and robots.txt files. The platform also provides page metadata settings and visitor analytics. Pre-rendering can help pages become crawlable, though it does not guarantee search engine indexing or rankings.


### **How does Floot's pricing compare to alternatives for professional use?**


Floot Pro costs[$25/month](https://floot.com/en/pricing) for the project owner. Teams should account for separate paid Floot plans when collaborators build through their own MCP connections, rather than assuming one subscription covers everyone. Floot Pro includes 12 mobile builds per month and a $10/month hosting allowance. Hosting usage beyond the included allowance incurs additional charges.
